Six thick, armoured legs end in large hooked claws and are splayed symmetrically. North: the same dome from behind. East: a side profile of a large oval, many-segmented abdomen with a small head at the right. The head has red eye clusters, two antennae and a thin beak angled down and forward with small palps. The legs are noticeably thinner and more spindly than on south and north. The east view has softer, more realistic rendering; south and north have a crisper outline and a more stylised, armoured look.

observed.east.png: The side profile at full resolution. A long oval abdomen with about 8 overlapping bands, finely textured and painterly. observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. Each shows a mass of saturated cobalt/sapphire crystal shards held in a dark navy, vein-like lattice, with pale teal curved hooks at the bottom or front. South is a roughly symmetric spiky cone with two big teal pincer hooks curving down and inward at the bottom centre. East is a long, low wedge of crystals sloping back to the left, with a cluster of teal hooks and two small antenna-like stalks at the right (front) end. North is a spiky pyramid of crystals with five or six smaller teal hooks fanning out along the bottom. None of the facings shows distinct walking legs, eyes or a readable head.
observed.south.png: A symmetric cluster of faceted blue crystals, with a tall central spike and smaller shards fanning out to the sides, bound by a dark blue root-like matrix. Two large teal sickle-shaped mandibles/pincers at the bottom curve toward each other. No eyes, no legs and no visible body under the crystals. Clean alpha. The rendering is smooth and glossy with hard facet planes, closer to a stylised mobile-game look than painterly.
observed.east.png: A side view of an elongated crystal mass lying low and diagonal, with long blue shards sweeping back and up to the left. At the right end are teal hooked mandibles, some smaller teal claws below them and two thin dark antenna stalks. Gaps in the dark lattice show through. No legs can be separated from the hooks. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: A pyramid of blue crystal shards over the dark lattice, with roughly six teal hooks spread along the lower edge, the outer ones curling outward. No eyes or face are drawn. The teal hooks look much like south's mandibles, so front and back are hard to tell apart. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the east sprite is about 2 cells long and about 1.3 cells tall, clearly bigger than the vanilla human. At 32 px/cell it shows as a blue spiky blob with a teal tip, about twice the human's footprint, and distinct from the brown ground.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the front: a symmetric view with the pair of large teal mandibles at the bottom centre facing the camera. No eyes are drawn, but the mouthparts mark it as the front.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North has no eyes or face. It does show a row of teal hooks along the bottom edge that look like south's mandibles, which makes the rear hard to read (see the F_INCONSISTENT finding). There is no face, so this item passes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are seen at an angle, and east is a true side profile. None is a top-down plan.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured spread is 19%. East is a long, low profile and south/north are tall cone fronts, so the shape changes with the pose. The overall bulk looks similar in facings.png.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The palette and crystal lattice match on every facing, but the teal appendages do not turn with the body. South has two large mandibles. North has about six smaller hooks spread along the bottom, as if it were showing the mouth end. East shows several hooks bunched at the front. No consistent set of legs is visible on any facing.

SIGNATURE.seen: A crystal/mineral creature is clearly shown, with crystal growths covering the body and big mandibles for eating rock.

ALIEN.seen: It does not read as an Earth mite or any Earth animal. It reads as an alien crystal creature, though as much a crystal cluster as an animal.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1 crystal facets jutting from the body: present, everywhere. 2 partly translucent stone-and-crystal hide: partial. It is saturated cobalt blue with teal, with no grey rock tone.

STYLE.seen: Smooth gradient facets, uniform glossy highlights and a clean graphic finish. This reads as a stylised mobile-game/vector render rather than painterly vanilla RimWorld. It is not cute, but it is not realistic either.

OURS.seen: Original art that does not match any vanilla or known donor animal.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out on the checkerboard on every facing, with no shadow or ground patch.

SCALE.seen: It is about 2 cells long, bigger than the human. The description gives no size words, only that it is a modified Pebblemit, and the Pebblemit's size is not shown. I cannot tell whether this much bulk is intended.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px it reads as a bold blue spiky shape with a teal front end, clearly separate from the brown ground. It reads as a creature mainly because of the teal tip.

reply.subject: RM_DecayDrake

observed.facings.png: Three facings on a checkerboard at one scale. South is a squat reptile seen head-on: a toad-like broad face with heavy brows, a huge round orange-red scaly throat or chest sac, four splayed clawed legs, and two dark membranous bat-like wings raised up and out on either side like flared ears. A spiked tail curls out to the left. East is a long, low, crocodile-like side profile with a long snout and an orange-tinted muzzle. A rounded red dewlap or throat sac hangs under the jaw. A row of spikes runs down the back and tail, and one fairly large membranous wing lies swept back along the back, partly raised. The flank and belly line is fairly slim. North shows the back of the head at the top with no eyes, a dorsal spike row running all the way down the spine and tail, both wings spread to the sides, the hind legs, and a long tail hanging down toward the bottom of the frame. It is noticeably taller than south.
observed.south.png: Front view of the same animal. It looks straight at the camera with low-lidded eyes and a frog- or toad-like mouth. The inflated orange throat or chest sac is the dominant shape. The wings are raised and flared above the shoulders. Clean alpha, no haze, no ground patch.
observed.east.png: Side profile. The body and tail are long and slender like a crocodile. The head has a long snout with an orange tip, and there is a red dewlap at the throat. The wing is medium-sized, membranous, mottled, and swept back over the body, held slightly raised rather than folded flat. The belly is not markedly distended. No mist from the mouth and no mash on the ground.
observed.north.png: Rear view. The back of the head is at the top with no face. The spine spike row is very prominent and runs the full length. Both wings are spread outward. The tail extends straight down toward the bottom edge, so the whole length of the back and tail is laid out vertically, which gives a partly overhead impression. The legs read as hind legs from behind.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature is about 2.5 cells long and about 1 cell tall, larger than the human. At 32 px per cell it reads as a long olive lizard or croc shape with a dark wing patch and a red throat spot, clearly apart from the ground.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face head-on with both eyes and the mouth toward the camera, and the chest sac forward.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back of the head, the spine and the tail. No eyes or face are visible.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: On north, the full spine and the tail run straight down the frame, as if seen from above. The body reads more as overhead or plan view than an angled rear view, and is much taller than the south view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured spread is 78%. North (194 px) is far taller than south (140 px). Some of that is the tail hanging toward the camera, but the north body and wings also look larger than on south.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Same olive scales, spike row, mottled membranous wings and tail on every facing. The wings turn with the body: flared to the sides on south and north, lengthwise on east.

SIGNATURE.seen: The description centres on a bloated belly and fermenting yeast breath. The swelling is a throat or chest sac, not a belly, the body in profile is slim, and there is no haze.

ALIEN.seen: In profile it reads as a winged crocodile with a frog's throat sac: a familiar Earth body with bat wings added.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1 stunted wings folded flat: ABSENT, the wings are medium-sized, raised and flared on south and north. 2 grossly bloated belly: ABSENT, the swelling is a throat or chest sac and the belly line in profile is slim. 3 yeast-mist haze from the mouth: ABSENT. 4 heavy squat drake frame: PARTIAL, south is squat but east is a long slender croc profile. 5 fermenting mash mounds: ABSENT.

STYLE.seen: Painterly scales and wing membrane, realistic shading and a thin dark outline. Not cel-shaded or photographic. The south face is slightly toad-like but not cute.

OURS.seen: Bespoke art matching the RM_ subject. It is not recognisable as a vanilla or other-mod animal.

ALPHA.seen: Real alpha on all facings with no ground, shadow or halo.

SCALE.seen: It is larger than the human and about 2.5 cells long, which fits a 'heavy' drake.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell it reads as a long olive body, a dark wing patch and a red throat spot.
